profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal planning meeting at a university-industry ML research lab to prepare a 6-week workshop submission and companion research note tentatively titled "The Foundations of Deep Learning with a Path Towards General Intelligence." The paper will synthesize deep learning's methodological assumptions, discuss failure modes, and argue for modularity and cognitive architecture extensions, with a small empirical appendix showing a toy modular-routing experiment. The agenda is to settle the paper structure, decide what empirical support is needed, divide writing and experiment responsibilities, and align on the timeline for an internal draft and submission package. The expected outcome is a concrete work plan covering the framing section, experiment setup, who owns the baseline runs, who prepares the reproducibility materials, and what must be ready by next week.

members.name: Dr. Lena Ortiz
members.expertise: theoretical deep learning, representation learning, and computational neuroscience
members.background: Lena leads the lab's long-horizon research agenda on general-purpose AI and often writes conceptual workshop papers that combine theory, synthesis, and a small illustrative empirical component.
members.private_state: She wants a clean, high-level argument that positions the lab early in the AGI foundations conversation without getting bogged down in a large experimental campaign, and she is worried that too much engineering work will delay the submission.
hidden_assumptions: When the lab says "the postulates," it refers to the seven-item framework from her invited seminar deck, because that is the version she has been publicly using.
A "baseline" for a conceptual workshop appendix is the last stable reference model the lab already trusts on compositional benchmarks, not necessarily the newest infrastructure default.
"Enough pilot evidence" means one convincing end-to-end run plus targeted qualitative analysis if the paper's core contribution is conceptual rather than benchmark-driven.
A "reproducibility package" means a tidy repo, configs, and instructions sufficient for another lab member to rerun the core figure later, not a submission-wide artifact bundle.

members.name: Ravi Chen
members.expertise: empirical deep learning, evaluation pipelines, and research infrastructure
members.background: Ravi joined from an industrial research group and is known for turning broad ideas into executable experiments with strong internal reproducibility standards and clean benchmark reporting.
members.private_state: He wants the project to look methodologically credible and reusable for future follow-up work, and he is concerned that a loosely specified appendix will create last-minute cleanup and fragile results.
hidden_assumptions: When people in the lab say "the postulates we used last time," they mean the four-axis condensed framework from the recent grant memo, because that is what current internal documents and shared notes use.
The "baseline" is whatever model/config is currently marked as the default reference in the active training repo, which is the retrieval-augmented Atlas-R branch.
"Enough pilot evidence" still implies the lab's normal minimum of multiple seeds and a compact summary table before calling a result fit for a paper, even if the paper is primarily conceptual.

A "reproducibility package" covers the full submission bundle—environment lockfile, figure scripts, processed artifacts, and run metadata—because otherwise the work cannot be cleanly handed off or extended.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to organize the draft around "the postulates" or "the postulates we used last time."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means the seven-postulate framework from her seminar deck on requirements for general-purpose AI.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means the four-axis framework from the lab's recent grant concept note and internal outline template.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both treat the framework as already established shared context, so the phrase sounds fully settled and neither has reason to enumerate the items during a short planning discussion.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Ravi will run the toy modular-routing idea against "the baseline."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means Atlas-125, the plain decoder-only transformer from last year's sanity suite that the lab has historically used for conceptual comparisons.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means Atlas-R, the newer retrieval-augmented default model in the current repo that engineering now labels as the standard baseline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both believe there is an obvious canonical baseline in the lab, and because they are discussing ownership rather than model choice, neither names the exact checkpoint or branch.

misalignment_points.topic: What is "enough pilot evidence" for the appendix
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the paper only needs "enough pilot evidence" or "a light empirical appendix."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes one successful run with a clear qualitative failure-mode comparison is enough to substantiate a conceptual claim for a workshop audience.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes "light" still means at least three seeds, mean/std reporting, and results on the two held-out compositional splits already in the lab's evaluation harness.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both explicitly downplay the empirical section as supportive rather than central, so the vague phrase feels safely aligned even though each maps it to different internal publication standards.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Ravi will put together the reproducibility package after the draft stabilizes.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this includes only the experiment code, configs, and a short README for reproducing the appendix figure.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this includes the full submission support bundle: environment pinning, figure-generation scripts, processed data artifacts, and archived run metadata for all paper plots and tables.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Artifact preparation is treated as a routine end-stage task, so they never enumerate the package contents; both hear a familiar phrase and project their own default scope onto it.

turns.inner_thought: I need this to stay a focused workshop piece: a strong conceptual argument about where current deep learning succeeds, where it breaks, and how modularity plus cognitive architecture ideas point toward more general intelligence. If we let the empirical tail wag the paper, we'll lose the six-week window. One illustrative appendix figure should be enough to make the claims feel grounded.
turns.utterance: I'd like us to keep this pretty tight. The main paper should frame the core assumptions behind deep learning, trace where those assumptions start to fray when you push toward general intelligence, and then motivate modularity and cognitive architecture as the natural extension. The empirical part should stay as a small appendix—just enough to make the story concrete.

turns.inner_thought: That works for me, as long as the conceptual arc is pinned to something structured enough that we can write and evaluate against it cleanly. I'll treat 'the postulates' as the four-axis framework from the grant memo, since that's what the current notes and templates use. And if we're saying light empirical appendix, I still want the usual minimum: multiple seeds and a compact table so this doesn't look hand-wavy.
turns.utterance: Yes, that makes sense. If we anchor the draft around the postulates and pair it with a lightweight experiment, I can help turn the conceptual arc into something concrete and easy to execute.

turns.utterance: Perfect. I'll take the foundations piece and the neuroscience synthesis, and I'd like you to draft the appendix narrative. Let's keep the empirical section compact and clearly in support of the main argument.

turns.inner_thought: That's fine, but I don't want us to end up with a brittle last-minute artifact scramble. turns.utterance: Sounds good. Once the appendix is stable, I'll also assemble the reproducibility package so the submission is easy to hand off and extend later.

turns.inner_thought: Next week I want a visible draft, not perfection. The postulates section should already be in near-presentable form using the seven-part framing, and one appendix figure should be enough to show momentum. If we have that, I can shape the rest quickly.
